method: Reconstructed the approved 180 EC from Article B4.1 and Appendices 1–2, cross-checked the duplicate and older-cohort transition, and read individual entry and disciplinary course evidence before retesting the no-match against the workbook.
findings: The adopted full-time table places Musical Celebrities only in year two. Its 42 EC elective allocation is split 24 EC in autumn and 18 EC in spring. The duplicate in the guide is not a separate credit-bearing course. The two 6 EC methods courses and the 6 EC research project are the current structure, and the replacement rules for earlier entrants do not apply.

Year one teaches music theory, both aural and harmony modules, music history and cultural and cognitive introductions. Later courses require positive binding study advice. Aural Skills I precedes Score Analysis, and a qualifying first-semester methods or score course precedes the research project. Computational Musicology, Cognitive Musicology and How Rhythm Works give 18 EC of the first listed variant. Completing the first two years and 30 EC in autumn of year three satisfies the 150 EC thesis gate.

The cultural trial includes genuine musical examples from Native American Histories and Media & Race and uses film, performance and media history for sound-related inquiry. It cannot sustain repertoire analysis, aural or harmony training, musical history or ethnomusicology. The cognition trial develops general perception, experiments, signal analysis and computing but offers no sequence in musical listening, timing, memory or computational study of music. Both 24-course schedules pass feasibility, so scheduling availability does not determine the result.
